## Folders: the flake vs your coursework

Two separate places, so the environment can be updated with `git` without
touching your work — and each course folder can be its own git repo:

```text
~/rsm-nix/                   the flake (a git repo) — RSM machinery only
                             update it with:  cd ~/rsm-nix && git pull

~/rsm-msba/                  your workspace (NOT a git repo)
├── .envrc                   generated; loads the flake from ~/rsm-nix
├── .rsm-msba/               RSM state (survives flake updates / re-clones)
│   ├── envs/nix-uv/         the "nix-uv" Python environment
│   ├── postgres/            your local PostgreSQL cluster
│   └── jupyter/             the "Python (nix-uv)" notebook kernel
├── examples/                link to the flake's examples
├── mgta403/                 a course folder — can be its own git repo
├── mgta464/
└── my_project/
```

direnv cascades the environment into every folder under `~/rsm-msba`, so the
tools are active in each course folder automatically. Because `~/rsm-msba` is
**not** a git repo, you can `git init` (or `git clone`) inside `mgta403` with no
nesting conflict.

Create more course/project folders any time:

```bash
rsm-new-course mgta455 mgta495
```

In VS Code, **File → Open Folder** on `~/rsm-msba`. With the direnv extension,
terminals and notebook kernels activate automatically. For notebooks, pick the
**"Python (nix-uv)"** kernel.
